threshold_origin: Fixed engineering thresholds declared before this feature extraction. They were not fitted on validation-event behavior or tuned to claim semantic accuracy. A threshold crossing creates a review candidate only.
observation_split_note: Observation validation retains whole source events. A text-training event may be held out separately for motion; it is not thereby an unseen text event.

text_review.basis: AI agent read the original publisher transcript, checked explicit questioner/respondent labels, selected contiguous turns and nearby conversational context. Caption onsets and interval end proxies were retained without acoustic verification. No human review is claimed.

limitations: Word timestamps are ASR estimates, not verified acoustic boundaries.
The original recording may contain edits; a candidate turn gap is not a validated pre-answer pause.
Speech rate includes pauses within the matched window and is not articulation rate.
Speech rate is not computed across unmatched or other-speaker words.

audible_laughter.reason: Visible smile scores and publisher stage directions cannot identify audible laughter by the respondent.

head_movement.reason: Head rotation candidates require camera/cut review before a nod or tilt can be assigned.

execution.scope: Recomputation from existing hashed ASR and visual model outputs; excludes original media acquisition/model inference. Shared-host timing is not an isolated throughput benchmark.

limitations: The pilot has only two observed events; correlated frames are not independent samples.
No human listening, acoustic-boundary review, image-to-speaker association, or semantic gesture accuracy is claimed.
Smiles are visual geometry candidates, audible laughter requires listening, and emotional state is never inferred.
Known camera-cut tails are excluded; camera-motion review remains required before accepting nod/tilt or hand gestures.
No raw interview text, original audio or video is copied into this report.
The language-specific speech units are not interchangeable; cross-language rate comparisons require a shared acoustic annotation method.
Candidate observations never automatically enter runtime voice or motion selection.
